(i) n- and e- but not i-NOS are expressed in motor neurons in the anterior horns, (ii) expression of NOS is not related to the severity of motor neuron loss in ALS, (iii) expression of NNOs in the motor neurons is approximately the same in all levels of spinal cord, and (iv) the expression of NNO in the motor neurons of the sacral cord is not different from that in the cervical cord
the expression of nitrite oxide synthases (n- and e-NOs) in anterior horn cells was increased in ALS.
the perikarya of motor neuron in ALS were immunoreactive for n- and i-NOS, but not for i-NOS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of N-O synthases in the motor neurons of the spinal cord.
a study of the expression of n- and e- but not i-NOS in the perikarya of motor neuron of ALS.
the expression of n- and e- NOSs in the anterior horn of the spinal cord of patients with ALS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of any involvement of n- and e- NOS in the pathogenesis of ALS.
NOSs are expressed by the perikarya of the motor neurons in ALS but that the expression of n- and e-nitric oxide synthases does not immediately affect the neuronal loss.
the expression of n- and e- NOSs in the motor neurons of spinal cord in ALS is not related to the severity of neuronal loss in the early stage of ALS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of i-NOS was not found in motor neurons of patients with ALS, and that the expression of n- and e- NOSs was found in motor neurons, but not in the normal controls.
NOSs may play a role in the late stage of ALS, but not immediately after neuronal degeneration.
NOSs are expressed in the motor neurons of the patients with ALS, and this expression is correlated to the severity of motor neuron loss in the anterior horn of ALS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NOSs, especially n- and e- NOSs, are expressed in the motor neurons of patients with ALS.
the expression of iNOS is increased in the motor neurons in ALS patients and that this expression may be involved in the pathogenesis of ALS.
the expression of n- and e- NOSs in the anterior horn neurons may be associated with the severity of the disease.
